cost.a: Every engagement starts with a free 30-minute diagnostic call. timing.q: How long until the agent is live?
timing.a: Most agents go live 3 to 4 weeks after kickoff. Up to 6 weeks if integrations are heavy or your data needs cleanup first. The diagnostic gives you the exact timeline (and the milestones) in writing before you commit to setup.

codeOwnership.a: No, and that's by design. Your agent runs on infrastructure we monitor and improve 24/7. You own everything that actually matters: your data, conversation history, integrations, business rules, and the agent's logic and tone. You can export all of it at any time. What you don't get is a codebase to maintain, hire for, or babysit. That's our job.

leaving.q: What if we want to leave?
leaving.a: Cancel any month after the first 3, with 30 days' notice. We export your data, conversation history and configuration in standard formats. If you're moving to another vendor, we help with the handoff. No clawbacks, no contractual lock-in.

compliance.q: Is our data safe? GDPR / CCPA?
compliance.a: Yes. EU-hosted infrastructure for European clients (GDPR-compliant by default). DPA signed before any real data touches our systems. Your data is never used to train models we sell to other clients. SOC 2 is on our roadmap; until then we share our security questionnaire and current controls under NDA.

channels.q: Which channels and tools do you integrate with?
channels.a: Out of the box: WhatsApp Business, Instagram DM, web chat, email, Google Calendar, Outlook, Stripe, Cal.com, HubSpot, common PMS / CRM / booking systems, and most no-code platforms (Make, n8n, Zapier). metrics.q: What do you actually measure, and how do we know it's working?

We measure them continuously and review them with you every improvement cycle, alongside conversation logs you can request at any time. If a metric drifts, the next improvement cycle prioritizes fixing it.

nda.a: Yes, but not for the first call. Our standard MSA + DPA cover most clients. We sign custom NDAs for regulated industries (healthcare, financial services, legal) on request, no friction.

different.q: How do we know you're different from another AI agency?
different.a: Two ways to test it. One: ask for a 15-minute reference call with a live client before you commit, and we'll arrange it. Two: the diagnostic itself. An agency that wants to sell at any cost doesn't tell clients to walk away. We do, when it's the right call. Shipping something the wrong client won't use is worse for both sides.

noNeed.q: What if the diagnostic concludes we don't need you?
noNeed.a: We tell you straight and you keep whatever notes and recommendations came out of the call to act on however you want: in-house, with another vendor, or shelved for later. We'd rather lose one deal than ship something that won't earn its keep. Long term, that's the only marketing that scales.

cancellation.title: Cancellation
cancellation.p1: You may cancel the managed service any month after the first three, with 30 days' written notice. There are no clawbacks and no contractual lock-in beyond the initial 3-month minimum.
cancellation.p2: On termination, we provide a 30-day export window during which we export your data, conversation history and configuration in standard formats. If you are moving to another vendor, we help with the handoff. After the export window, we delete all client data except what we are legally required to retain.

confidentiality.title: Confidentiality and NDAs
confidentiality.p1: Both sides treat the other's confidential information as confidential, period. Our standard MSA covers this for most engagements. We sign custom NDAs for regulated industries (healthcare, financial services, legal) on request, with no friction.

sla.title: Service levels
sla.p1: Each tier ships with an incident-response commitment, written into the contract. Business 360 includes a 4-hour response window for production incidents.
sla.p2: We measure outcome metrics agreed during the diagnostic (response time, resolution rate, no-shows recovered). We review them with you every improvement cycle. If a metric drifts, the next improvement cycle prioritises fixing it.

liability.title: Liability
liability.p1: Our aggregate liability is capped at the fees paid to Auphere in the twelve months preceding the claim. We exclude indirect and consequential damages to the extent permitted by law.
liability.p2: These caps do not apply to indemnities for confidentiality breaches, willful misconduct or the breach of data protection obligations. The MSA spells out the carve-outs.

law.title: Governing law
law.p1: Unless your MSA says otherwise, these terms are governed by the law of Spain. EU clients may elect to be governed by the law of their habitual residence for consumer-protection purposes.

meta.description: How Auphere isolates client data, where it lives, who can touch it, and what we do when something goes wrong.

header.title: Compliance-by-design. Not check-the-box.
header.intro: Where data lives, how tenants are isolated, what gets encrypted, who can touch what, and what happens when something goes wrong. The architecture, not the marketing.

hosting.title: Where data lives
hosting.p1: Our production runtime is hosted on infrastructure in the European Union by default. EU clients get EU-only processing on request, with the exception of vendors that do not offer an EU region (those are listed in the privacy policy with their region).
hosting.p2: US-only or LATAM-only processing is available for clients with regulatory requirements that demand it, on a per-contract basis.

rls.description: Each tenant's data is partitioned at the database level. Tenant context is scoped automatically on every query. Application code cannot accept a tenant ID from a caller, by design.

tools.description: Each agent ships with an explicit allow-list of tools and integrations. Even if a model tried to call something outside the list, the runtime rejects the call before it hits a third party.

models.description: Your conversation data is never used to train models we sell to other clients. We use zero-retention APIs with our LLM providers.

encryption.title: Encryption
encryption.p1: All data is encrypted in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest (AES-256 on managed-database storage). Secrets are managed in Doppler and rotated on a schedule.
encryption.p2: Backups are encrypted with the same controls and retained for 30 days.

access.title: Who can access what
access.p1: Access to client data is restricted to the engineers actively delivering or supporting that client's agent: a small, named list per engagement. All access is logged.
access.p2: Engineers use named accounts, hardware MFA and short-lived credentials. No shared accounts. No password reuse across systems.

gdpr.description: EU-hosted by default. DPA signed before any real data touches our systems. Sub-processors listed in the privacy policy.

ccpa.description: We do not sell personal information. California residents can exercise CCPA rights via contacto@auphere.com.

lgpd.description: Brazilian clients can request LGPD-aligned processing: same operational guarantees as GDPR, contract amendments as needed.

soc2.description: Not yet started: certification is on our roadmap. In the meantime, we share our security questionnaire and current controls on request, under NDA.

aitransparency.title: AI transparency (EU AI Act, Article 50)
aitransparency.p1: Every Auphere agent identifies itself as AI from the first message, on every channel. It is a design obligation under Article 50 of the EU AI Act, applicable since August 2, 2026: on voice, the agent says it at the start of the call; on text channels, in its introduction. We do not design agents to pass as human, and we decline configurations that ask for it.
aitransparency.p2: When the agent cannot or should not resolve something, it escalates to a human with the full context of the conversation. Human escalation ships enabled by default — it is also what Spain's Ley 10/2025 will require of customer-service bots from December 28, 2026.

subprocessors.title: Sub-processors
subprocessors.p1: The full, up-to-date list of sub-processors is published in our privacy policy with the region and purpose for each one. We notify clients in advance of any change.

incident.title: If something goes wrong
incident.p1: We commit to notify affected clients of any confirmed security incident within 72 hours of discovery, with what we know at that point and how we are responding.
incident.p2: We run blameless postmortems for any production incident with material impact and share the relevant findings with clients.

vuln.title: Reporting a vulnerability
vuln.p1: If you believe you have found a security issue, write to contacto@auphere.com with subject [security]. We acknowledge within 1 business day, fix verified issues without ceremony, and credit reporters who want the recognition.

capabilities.headline: What your agent already knows how to do.
capabilities.intro: Nothing on this list is roadmap. All of it is in production today.

media.title: Understands voice notes and photos, not just text
media.body: The audio and photos your customers send, understood and answered.
media.detail: It transcribes voice notes and reads the images that arrive on WhatsApp or Instagram: the payment receipt, the product photo, the two-minute audio with the whole story. Your customer writes how they write; the agent adapts.

memory.title: Remembers every customer between conversations
memory.body: Today's conversation knows what happened last month.
memory.detail: Per-customer memory: preferences, history, context. It is the only thing on this list your customer directly perceives — and what turns a bot into an agent.

jobs.title: Books, reminds, chases unpaid bills and recovers no-shows — on its own
jobs.body: The four jobs that burn the most hours, with nobody pushing them.
jobs.detail: Bookings with confirmation and one-tap rescheduling, reminders that cut no-shows, calm payment follow-ups and win-back of absent customers. Each flow activates only if your operation needs it.

browser.title: Uses your software even if it has no API
browser.body: If your management tool only has a screen, the agent uses it anyway.
browser.detail: An agent-operated browser session books in your legacy panel exactly as a person would. The software you already run stops being an excuse.

escalation.title: Knows when to stay quiet and hand off to a person
escalation.body: Three triggers, full context, a named inbox.
escalation.detail: Out of scope, explicit request, or low confidence: the agent escalates to your team with the whole conversation. It is also what Spain's Ley 10/2025 requires from December — your agent already complies.

hygiene.title: Watches your number's standing with Meta
hygiene.body: The real fear of operating WhatsApp, managed by default.
hygiene.detail: Number-quality monitoring, approved templates and a sending cadence that trips no alarms. A burned number is a dead channel: we treat it as part of the service.
